caption: A kitchen scene shows an oven with its door open, emitting thick black smoke and flames, with a smoke detector on the ceiling having its red light on.
emergency_response: Immediately close the oven door to cut off oxygen supply to the flames. Turn off the oven to eliminate the heat source. If the fire is small and contained, use a kitchen-rated fire extinguisher (Class B or K), aiming at the base of the flames. If the fire persists or is uncontrollable, evacuate everyone from the home immediately and call 911. Do not use water on the fire as this could worsen it, especially if it's a grease fire. Once safely outside, wait for emergency services to arrive. After the fire is extinguished, ventilate your home to remove smoke.

caption: In the image, three people seated in an airplane cabin are using oxygen masks, with several others in the background doing the same. Some of the overhead compartments are open, with luggage on the verge of falling out, indicating an emergency situation.
emergency_response: Immediately secure your oxygen mask properly before helping others, even children. Remain seated with your seatbelt fastened and do not attempt to secure falling luggage during this cabin depressurization emergency. The pilot is performing an emergency descent to a safe altitude (around 10,000 feet) where normal breathing is possible. Though the oxygen supply lasts approximately 12 minutes, the descent typically takes only 4-5 minutes, ensuring sufficient oxygen. Keep the mask on until the crew indicates it's safe to remove it. Stay calm, follow all flight attendant instructions, and prepare for possible turbulence during the rapid descent.

caption: A fire is engulfing a living room, with flames visibly consuming the area around a television on a stand and a smaller fire on a coffee table, as seen through a window framed by curtains, alongside a sofa and a lit lamp.
emergency_response: Evacuate the home immediately - do not attempt to extinguish this large, spreading fire. Close doors behind you if possible to slow fire spread, but don't delay your exit. Once safely outside, call 911 immediately and clearly report the house fire. Maintain a safe distance from the burning structure and ensure all household members are accounted for. Do not under any circumstances re-enter the burning building, even for pets or valuables. Alert neighbors if the fire could spread to their properties. When firefighters arrive, provide information about anyone potentially trapped inside and any hazardous materials in the home. Follow all instructions from emergency personnel at the scene.
